THE SYNOD OF PENNSYLVANIA-WEST VIRGINIA
OF THE UNITED PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
3040 MARKET STREET
CAMP HILL, PA. 17011
(717) 737-0421
July 26, 1973
Mr. George Jennings
Dauphin County Planning Commission
2001 North Front Street
Harrisburg, Pa.
Dear Mr. Jennings:
I have reviewed the Harrisburg Redevelopment Plan which you submitted and while these comments do not represent an official response of the total committee, I believe they would follow fairly accurately the present knowledge and experience of the committee. The plan would seem to comprehend difficulties in the development of resources and services in the Harrisburg community particularly in regard to housing. It is our opinion that for peculiar and somewhat different reasons, residential development and related environmental effects may be of a nature related specifically to the Harrisburg Community.
Concerning the housing inventory and its potential need, a planning approach is possible due to the fact that there are critical needs but not desperate as to forego an orderly process. Both non-profit and local realtors are aware that usable housing exists within the city and related municipalities, but that crisis factors relate more to sales appeal, credit services, and uncertain neighborhood factors, rather than a shortage of housing.
Characteristics of the population due to occupation and income structure of a major governmental have made total community consensus difficult over the past and will present problems in the future. The consent of necessary segments of the community to let an orderly disposition of housing coccur presents problems, but these seem in a way to be anticipated by the Plan.
The Housing Council and other organizations concerned with the problems of housing would probably like to see some rather massive help emerging from Federal or State sources to energize citizen effort in what is beyond their own capacity. It is our belief that while the business community is essential defects in the housing delivery system have not been adequately dealt with. It is perhaps to be expected, but the Plan would seem to need development in this area at some future time.
Sincerely, Souleu traler
Joseph E. Grottenthaler
Chairman of the Housing Committee
